messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT CREATED • KV-cache/continuous-batching perf cliff detected (auto-alert)

anna_oncall: seeing huge tail latency and token cost spike across us-west-2 dedicated pools. Started at ~15:12 UTC. Traffic steady but 95p latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.3s.

anna_oncall: metrics: kv_cache_used_bytes up 4x, kv_cache_frag_ratio ~78%, alloc failures on a few nodes. stack traces show repeated cudaMalloc failures.

liam_eng_runtime: can you paste the logs? do we have OOMs or just allocation slowdowns?

anna_oncall: logs from runtime-rl-3:
```
2026-03-15T15:14:02Z runtime: alloc: cudaMalloc returned error out of memory
2026-03-15T15:14:02Z kv_cache: fragment_ratio=0.783 free_chunks=120 used_chunks=5400
2026-03-15T15:14:03Z batching: continuous_batch.max_tokens=2048 inflight_batches=16
2026-03-15T15:14:04Z perf: p99_latency_ms=2310
```

liam_eng_runtime: hm, continuous batching + high kv cache churn -> fragmentation blowup. Could be allocator arenas not releasing memory back to CUDA driver, causing OOMs and long stalls.

liam_eng_runtime: quick mitigation plan:
- reduce continuous batching max_tokens to limit KV growth
- enable KV compaction/eviction aggressive policy
- restart a subset of runtimes after env tweak (PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF)
- notify customers and start handoff

anna_oncall: doing step 1 now — patching via console API to update route config for the v2-model group.

anna_oncall: curl snippet I ran:
```
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/configs/route/update \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -d '{"route":"/v2/generate","continuous_batch.max_tokens":512}'
```

ops-bot: CONFIG PATCH SUCCESS • route=/v2/generate continuous_batch.max_tokens set to 512 (applied to 27/27 hosts)

anna_oncall: immediately saw a drop in new kv allocations on the patched hosts. p95 latency down to ~300ms within 90s.

jordan_prod: customer impact: we flagged 12 customers hitting Dedicated capacity limits, 2 reported degraded responses (slower but not errors). No widespread 500s.

liam_eng_runtime: next I'm going to enable kv compaction and set a more conservative arena policy on a canary node. Command:
```
# set PyTorch CUDA split size and enable compaction
export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64
# enable runtime kv compaction
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/configs/kv_compact \
  -d '{"enabled":true,"threshold_pct":60,"interval_sec":90}'
```

liam_eng_runtime: canary applied to runtime-rl-3b. Monitoring for 5m.

maya_sre: taking over on-call in 30m. please summarize current state and blockers for handoff.

anna_oncall: summary for handoff ->
- root symptom: KV cache fragmentation + continuous batching expansion during sustained token per-request increase -> allocation failures and perf cliff
- mitigations applied: reduced continuous_batch.max_tokens 2048->512 across v2 endpoints, enabled canary kv compaction, restarted 6/27 hosts to clear fragmented arenas
- immediate effect: p95/p99 improved, kv allocation rate down 70% on patched hosts
- open actions: 1) full rollout of kv compaction if canary stable 2) engineering investigation into allocator behavior and arena tuning 3) customer comms draft (jordan)

maya_sre: noted. I'll continue monitoring for next 2h. escalate to eng-runtime if canary shows >10% error or kv_frag >65% again.

liam_eng_runtime: flagged a follow-up bug: ENG-RUNTIME-3421 "cuda malloc arena fragmentation under continuous-batching". initial hypotheses: caching allocator max_split_size or glibc arena settings cause long-lived free segments that can't be coalesced.

liam_eng_runtime: suggested longer-term fixes: adaptive batch shaping (cap tokens based on current free_kv), proactive compaction during low qps, and revise default PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF to `max_split_size_mb:64` with testing.

jordan_prod: customer comms: drafting note to affected customers: "We've mitigated the latency spike by throttling batch sizes and applying cache compaction. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with a timeline for a permanent fix." will post to status page in 15m if no regression.

ops-bot: ROLLING RESTART: initiated restart for 6 hosts to release fragmented arenas (hosts: runtime-rl-3a,b,c, runtime-rl-7a,b,c). ETA 4m.

anna_oncall: restarts completed. verification: p99 back to <400ms, kv_frag_ratio down to 42% on restarted hosts.

maya_sre: handoff notes -> keep an eye on: kv_frag_ratio, cudaMalloc errors, continuous_batch inflight_batches. Thresholds:
- alert if kv_frag_ratio > 60%
- alert if cudaMalloc errors > 3/min
- paging: escalate to eng-runtime with link to ENG-RUNTIME-3421

liam_eng_runtime: I'll pick up full investigation tomorrow morning (UTC). will run heap profiling and instrument allocator stats. probable next steps include adding a periodic compaction pass and testing arena/alloc conf changes under load.

maya_sre:Thanks all. I'll update the incident ticket with timeline and close the active paging if metrics remain stable for 1h. leaving this thread open for any late regressions. :white_check_mark:

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED • status=monitoring • severity=major • incident_link=https://incidents.internal/1762001234
